case_name: M.G. Bhide vs Britannia Industries Ltd., Mayur ... on 23 March, 2005
facts_of_case: Complaint (ULP) No. 416 of 1996 filed by the petitioner before the Industrial Court at Pune, praying for declaration that the respondent company had engaged in acts of unfair labour practices and that the complainant was permanent employee of respondent no.1 from 1.7.1997.

legal_principles.principle: The power of superintendence conferred by Article 227 of the Constitution is to be exercised more sparingly and only in appropriate cases.
legal_principles.held: the Supreme Court held that the power of superintendence conferred by Article 227 of the Constitution is to be exercised more sparingly and only in appropriate cases

legal_principles.principle: The exercise of jurisdiction under Article 227 is limited and restrictive in nature.
legal_principles.held: Their Lordships stated thus: 'Generally speaking the exercise of jurisdiction under Article 227 of the Constitution is limited and restrictive in nature.'

legal_principles.principle: A finding of fact is not open to correction by the High Court unless it is a perverse recording or not based on any material whatsoever resulting in manifest injustice.
legal_principles.held: except where it is a perverse recording thereof, or not based on any material whatsoever resulting in manifest injustice
cited_cases: Surya Dev Rai v. Ram Chander Rai

legal_principles.principle: The jurisdiction to exercise supervisory powers is not available for indulging in reappreciation or evaluation of evidence or correcting the errors in drawing inferences like a Court of appeal.
legal_principles.held: the jurisdiction to exercise supervisory powers is not available for indulging in reappreciation or evaluation of evidence or correcting the errors in drawing inferences like a Court of appeal
cited_cases: Surya Dev Rai v. Ram Chander Rai
